claims.claim: The Ocarina of Time remake sold over 5.2 million units worldwide in its first four days after launching November 5, 2026.
810,000 of those units were sold in Japan.
It is the highest global four-day sales for any Nintendo-published Switch 2 game.
Insider Gaming's review said veterans might find the remake too easy.
The $520 40th Anniversary Edition console does not include the game.
The game costs $60 digitally and $70 on a physical cartridge.
Retailers ran out of the Zelda console and scalping rose.

issues.quote: A 1998 classic beat every new launch
issues.problem: The on-screen text drops the qualifier. The sources only say it was the best four-day start for a Nintendo-published Switch 2 game, not every launch. The spoken script carries the qualifier correctly.

check.summary: The sources support every factual claim: 5.2M units in four days (810,000 in Japan), the record for a Nintendo-published Switch 2 game, the 96 Metacritic score, the $520 console that doesn't include the game, $60 digital and $70 cartridge pricing, and Insider Gaming's 'too easy for veterans' remark. The 1998 original release is established public knowledge. Opinions are clearly framed as opinion. The only issue is a slightly over-broad on-screen line.
